description: Design pins the "this pane" section at the top of the catalog, followed by GLOBAL; code keeps Agent run in its normal catalog slot (after Lists) and scrolls the list to it, so the view starts at AGENT RUN and GLOBAL is out of sight
note: [section-order] the board's own caption says "NOT pinned … auto-scrolls to it on open", so the artboard contradicts its caption

description: Shortcut rows come from the live command registry: Agent run has about 40 rows (Where this runs, Session actions, Focus composer input, Model effort and speed …) instead of the design's 8 samples; Surface a card and Archive agent are not there, Toggle important / Copy bee id / self-seal are far below, notes are reworded ("running bee: queued, delivered at turn end"), and GLOBAL lacks Jump to pane, Jump to most important, Needs me
note: [catalog-content] design shows sample data; code renders the registry as extracted by the capture fixture (which misses plugin contributions and has no availability predicates), so part of this row may be fixture-only

description: Command names are cut off with an ellipsis when the note is long ("Where this …", "Session actio…", "Queue until the current turn e…", "Work…", "Scroll transcript down / up half a …"); in the design the name always shows in full and only the note gives way
note: [label-truncation] label span can shrink as much as the note; long registry notes squeeze it

description: Section header reads "THIS PANE · AGENT RUN" followed by a mono "· opened from drone-07" in design; code shows "AGENT RUN" with a small grey "THIS PANE" pill and no "opened from" origin
note: [this-pane-header] matches the caption's "neutral this-pane tag"; origin text dropped

description: The this-pane rows sit in a bordered rounded card (1px #ECEAE5, 8px radius) in design; code has no card, so the rows are flush with the rest of the list
Guide sidebar is 216px wide in code vs 253px in design, so the search field, the list and the esc cap all start 37px further left
note: [sidebar-width] design is 232px + padding + border (content-box); code is narrower even beyond the box model

description: Guide topic "Yards & quests" reads "Yards & products" in code
Guide topic "Loops" is missing from the sidebar
"What's new 0.4.2" and "About Apiary" at the bottom of the sidebar are missing
Sidebar group labels and topics sit about 6px higher (GUIDE text y≈59 vs 66, Getting started y≈86 vs 92); group label blocks are spaced differently
Footer hints "type to search · ↑↓ move · ↵ run command · esc close" and their separators are missing; only "click keys to rebind" and "live from the command registry" remain
Count reads "183 shortcuts · 14 surfaces" instead of "86 bindings · 10 surfaces"
Anchor rail lists the code's 14 surfaces: adds Browser, Terminal, Whiteboard, Tracks, Agent run, Inbox, Sheet; has no This pane, Changes or Sidebar & pickers; Editor is "Files & editor"
Active anchor styling differs: design highlights "This pane" in primary ink #2E2B27 (600) with "Global" in #6F6B63; code highlights "Agent run" in #6F6B63 (600) and "Global" is faint like the rest
Anchor rail is 128px wide vs 163px and its items are spaced 22.7px apart vs 21px
When a command has several key groups, code puts a faint "·" between the caps ("⌃. · ⌘.", "⇥ · ⌘⌥F"); design just spaces the caps 3px apart

Boxes with borders are smaller in code because the design adds borders outside the authored size and code includes them: key caps 18px vs 21px tall (label sits 1.5px higher), search field 34px vs 36px, footer 34px vs 35px, card 1060×716 vs 1062×718
note: [box-sizing] same cause as Keycap [cap-height]: content-box in design, border-box in code

description: Key-cap label ink is lighter in code: #6B6862 (inkSoft) vs #5A564E
Key caps use border #E2E0DB (ghostBorder) instead of --color-border #E7E5E0
Dialog shadow is lighter and tighter in code: 0 16px 40px rgba(40,35,30,.15) vs --shadow-panel 0 24px 64px rgba(40,35,30,.30); only a 4px strip of it shows inside the card-only capture
The focused search field has a darker border in code (#DAD5CC) than the dialog design shows for it (--color-border #E7E5E0, while the design already paints a caret, i.e. focused)
note: [search-focus-border] code's focus style; the board's own search state (n147) uses #DAD5CC
